subject: Interim advisory: transient routing regression impacting API availability
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Interim advisory: transient routing regression impacting API availability

Hi Amit / Sierra Ops team,

Quick advisory from Redwood Inference — we're seeing a transient routing regression that caused elevated 502s and slowed inference responses for a subset of requests to the hosted text-generation API beginning ~08:05 UTC. We've engaged the on-call runbook and routed affected traffic to an alternate pool to reduce impact.

What we know so far:
- Symptoms: intermittent 502s and >2s tail latency for ~1.8% of requests to your production endpoints.
- Incident start: ~08:05 UTC; automated fallback triggered at 08:09 UTC.
- Current state: routing rollback applied; majority of traffic restored to normal. Some requests may still see occasional slow tails while caches warm.

Immediate customer-facing actions we've taken:
- Fallback routing enabled to avoid retries and timeouts.
- Increased capacity on dedicated pools for your service while we validate stability.
- Posted a short note on the status page and will update as we confirm full resolution. (link below)

Attachments: status_snapshot_20271002.png (PNG of a brief status page snapshot)

Next update: 30 minutes, or sooner if we have a resolution and full mitigation confirmation.

Sorry for the disruption — we know this is time-sensitive for you. Ben and Marissa are on the bridge and will follow with technical details and a remediation timeline.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Interim advisory: transient routing regression impacting API availability

Hi Amit — quick technical summary from the bridge:

Root cause (preliminary): an automated config rollout for the global request router incorrectly applied a KV-to-pool affinity rule for a small routing subset. The rule caused a fraction of in-flight requests to be sent to an under-provisioned cache shard, leading to increased tail latency and a higher 502 surface.

What we did to remediate:
- Immediate rollback of the rollout at 08:09 UTC, which rebalanced traffic across healthy pools.
- Engaged the dedicated pool for Sierra Health and pre-warmed the KV cache to suppress tail latency.
- Added temporary sticky-routing guard to prevent the misapplied affinity rule from reappearing during reconfig windows.

Impact assessment (prelim):
- Peak error rate: ~1.8% of requests over a 7-minute window (08:05–08:12 UTC).
- PII-sensitive routes: no evidence of failed logs being sent to external sinks; all failures occurred before any response bodies were emitted. We will confirm via audit log query and include evidence in the postmortem.

I'm attaching a short log excerpt that highlights the routing decision errors for the window (kv-routing-log-snippet.txt).

We will draft the full root cause and mitigations and share a customer-facing postmortem by EOD +2 business days. If you'd like an immediate bridge to walk through the technicals and impact, we can meet within the hour.

Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: routing regression — incident resolved, next steps

Amit / team,

Update from operations: the rollout rollback and pool rebalancing completed by 09:02 UTC and we've seen normal request success rates since ~09:10 UTC. We've closed the active bridge.

Customer next steps we will take:
- Postmortem: customer-facing summary + technical appendix by 2027-10-04 EOD (internal ticket INC-2027-102).
- Evidence: we'll include targeted audit log excerpts showing failed request ids and timestamps; those will be redact-ready for PII.
- Credits: our account team will propose a service credit for the affected window; Laura, can you pick this up with Sierra's billing contact?
- Preventive actions: scheduled hardening to the rollout guard and a new canary window for global router config changes.

We realize this affected your production traffic during a critical window. We will follow up with a short call to walk through the appendix if you'd like.

Thanks for the quick coordination.

— Marissa
